04. The current status of Viet Nam's
rubber industry in relation to the EUDR
4.1. Challenges
4.1.1. Smallholder

(a) Smallholder rubber is becoming increasingly important in Viet Nam's rubber processing industry. However, it 
involves hundreds of thousands of households, each with small, scattered plots that may grow various types of trees
(b) Most smallholder plantations lack geolocation for their production plots

(c) Information about the EUDR is still "new" to most smallholders, many of whom are either not interested in or do 
not fully understand its requirements
(d) Smallholders do not typically collect or store information on latex production and trade transactions

(e) Latex from a smallholder can be sold to various buyers, but without an information-sharing mechanism, 
traceability of raw rubber becomes increasingly dicult down the supply chain
(f) Some smallholders (and enterprises) are not willing to share/provide information

(g) Smallholders hire workers based on verbal agreements, without formal contracts, and there is unclear 
information regarding the use of child or underage labour

(h) Some smallholders lack legal documents proving ownership of their rubber plantations, and the land is still 
disputed with unclear boundaries
4.1.2. Raw rubber traders
(d) Labour use without labour contracts
(e) Some local traders may not be ocially registered
4.1.3. Enterprises involved in estate rubber growing, processing, and exporting

(b) The number of rubber enterprises actively working 
to meet the EUDR remains low

(c) Many enterprises are aware of the EUDR, but their 
understanding remains limited
(g) There are some misconceptions about the EUDR
4.1.4. Management agencies
(a) No Forest Status Map as of 31 December 2020

(b) The rubber industry in Viet Nam is managed by multiple ministries. However, apart from MAE, other relevant 
ministries show limited interest in preparing to comply with the EUDR
(c) Local authorities have had limited access to information about the EUDR and show low levels of interest
(d) Lack of funding for implementation
(e) Lack of specific guidance for EUDR compliance
4.2. Some positive factors
(a) Some national agencies have stepped in and implemented activities
(b) Support from international organisations

(c) Rubber trees currently tapped for latex are not 
related to deforestation

(d) Most rubber plantations have legal ownership 
documentation

(e) Existing infrastructure facilitates EUDR alignment 
for enterprises

(f) Transaction information is stored long-term by 
processors

(g) Enterprises comply with labour law, labour rights, 
and environmental protection regulations

(h) Non-EU customers request EUDR-compliant 
rubber

(i) Abundant and various digital platforms and 
software for information management

(j) Several enterprises have pioneered EUDR 
compliance in their activities

(k) Customer support for enterprises to align with 
EUDR requirements

(l) Enterprise support through the linkage model may 
help smallholders meet EUDR requirements
